channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Resultado das eleições 2026: Bolsa bate recorde histórico e dólar cai abaixo de R$ 5
item.description: The 2026 elections triggered a strong market reaction driven by expectations of a more orthodox economic policy under a potential Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) government, currently leading polls ahead of a possible October 25 runoff against Lula. Economy and fiscal stability dominate the debate, with investors reacting to potential changes in public accounts.

item.title: Número de militares entre candidatos eleitos cresce em relação a 2022
item.description: The number of elected military candidates in 2026 reached 53, marking a significant increase from the 33 elected in 2022. This growth reflects the rising influence of the armed forces in Brazilian political circles. Results may still see minor adjustments after the second-round vote scheduled for October 25th.

item.title: Quem zerou na eleição? 7 candidatos não receberam nem o próprio voto
item.description: Seven candidates for state deputy received zero votes in the first round of the 2026 elections, according to TSE data. The names appear in official results from five states, highlighting low visibility or voter rejection.

item.title: Urnas punem Gilmar, Dino e Moraes
item.description: The first round of elections showed that the performance of Supreme Court justices significantly influenced popular voting. Surveys indicate that Gilmar Mendes, Alexandre de Moraes, and Flávio Dino had relevant impact on electoral decisions.

item.title: Milei dá parabéns a Tarcísio de Freitas e critica pesquisas do Brasil
item.description: Argentine President Javier Milei congratulated Tarcísio de Freitas and Flávio Bolsonaro, criticizing Brazilian electoral polls as 'political fraud' that misrepresent reality. Milei emphasized support for freedom in Brazil and expects bilateral cooperation with right-wing governments. His statements reinforce ideological alignment with Brazilian conservative figures.

item.title: Valdemar diz que Bolsonaro pode ser "forte candidato" à Presidência em 2030
item.description: The president of the PL, Valdemar Costa Neto, stated that Jair Bolsonaro could be a strong presidential candidate in 2030, depending on Flávio Bolsonaro's election. He noted that the former president is serving house arrest for involvement in a coup plot, but emphasized enduring popular support.

item.title: Rio das Flores, Valença, Niterói e mais: veja as cidades com vitória de Lula no RJ
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) won Rio de Janeiro with 53.01% of the votes, while Lula (PT) secured victories in only 9 of the state's 92 cities, notably in Rio das Flores (57.10%). Despite pockets of support, Lula faces strong opposition in the state.

item.title: Terceiro colocado, Cury fala em manter “silêncio” no segundo turno
item.description: Third-place candidate Augusto Cury (Avante) said he will remain silent regarding the runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, not authorizing any endorsement in his name. He also announced plans to leave political life, ending a campaign against polarization and calling for dialogue and unity. Cury thanked voters and urged proposals for a hopeful government.

item.title: Com 109 deputadas eleitas, bancada feminina cresce 21,1% na Câmara
item.description: The female caucus in the Chamber of Deputies grows by 21.1%, increasing from 90 to 109 parliamentarians, with the PT, PCdoB, and PV federation leading with 34 elected women. Despite the growth, women hold only 21% of the 513 seats, while men occupy 79%. States like São Paulo, Minas Gerais, and Rio de Janeiro lead in electing female deputies, though some states, such as the Federal District and Piauí, did not elect any women.

item.title: Eleições em Conceição do Coité (BA): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: In Conceição do Coité (BA), Lula (PT) leads the presidential race with 58.84% of votes, followed by Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) with 37.13%. Acm Neto (UNIÃO) wins the gubernatorial race with 49.97%, nearly tied with Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) at 49.79%. Contests for Senate, Chamber of Deputies, and State Assembly were also held with results reported.

item.title: Saiba os candidatos a presidente com maior e menor ‘custo por voto’ recebido
item.description: Among presidential candidates, Augusto Cury and Rui Costa Pimenta had the lowest cost per vote, while Romeu Zema and Ronaldo Caiado recorded the highest. Based on the first round and campaign expenses, Zema spent R$ 15.86 per vote and Caiado, R$ 8.45. Cury invested R$ 0.16 per voter and Pimenta, R$ 0.02. Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula had similar costs, around R$ 1.20 per vote.

item.title: Saiba quem são os candidatos ao Senado menos votados em cada UF
item.description: Poder360 ranked the 2026 Senate candidates with the lowest votes, highlighting Cloves José (PCO) from Piauí, who received only 634 votes and has his registration under judicial review. Several candidates had votes annulled under judicial scrutiny due to rejected electoral registrations, as per TSE guidelines.

item.title: Fandoms de Beyoncé a Anitta 'entregam' perfis nas redes para campanha de Lula; entenda
item.description: Fan communities of artists like Beyoncé, Anitta, Taylor Swift, and BTS have handed over social media profiles to support Lula's campaign after the first round of the 2026 elections, where Flávio Bolsonaro leads with 47.03% against Lula's 45.16%. The move aims to mobilize non-voters and undecided voters for the runoff on October 25, promoting democracy and civic engagement.

item.title: Celina Leão não foi eleita no primeiro turno por 168 votos
item.description: Celina Leão (PP) and Leandro Grass (PT) advanced to a runoff in the Federal District elections, with the sitting governor missing victory in the first round by just 168 votes. Leão attributed the narrow miss to a 'won already' sentiment and pledged to court new voters, while Grass emphasized the need to consolidate support for the good of Brasília.

item.title: Áudio: Eleição mobiliza eleitores brasileiros em 134 países
item.description: Brazilian voters abroad cast their ballots in 186 cities across 134 countries, using electronic voting machines in cities such as Paris, London, and Milan, except in Moscow, where paper voting was used due to delayed equipment delivery. Voting proceeded peacefully despite long lines in some cities. The process showcases the organization of the judiciary and the Superior Electoral Court to ensure Brazilians' right to vote overseas.

item.title: Flávio aposta em governadores eleitos para buscar votos nos estados no segundo turno, enquanto falta de palanques preocupa Lula
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) intends to leverage newly elected governors to strengthen his second-round campaign, while Lula's team is concerned about the lack of PL governors supporting them. The PL secured five governors and is activating allies to boost presence across states. The PT's campaign faces structural limitations due to having elected only three governors so far.

item.title: Eleições 2026: 7 candidatos não receberam nenhum voto
item.description: Seven candidates for legislative positions received zero votes in the 2026 elections, according to a Poder360 survey based on TSE data. Two of them, from the Mobiliza party, had their candidacies annulled sub judice and also received no votes. The remaining candidates were defeated without electoral support.

item.title: São Pedro da Aldeia, Casimiro de Abreu, Búzios, Petrópolis e mais: veja as cidades com vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro no RJ
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) won the first round of the presidential election in Rio de Janeiro, winning in 83 out of 92 cities in the state. He led with 53.01% of the votes (4,966,844), surpassing Luiz Inácio Lula from PT, who obtained 39.41% (3,693,021 votes).

item.title: Resultados de las elecciones en Brasil, en vivo| La Bolsa de São Paulo y el real reciben con subidas la victoria parcial de Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (47.03%) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (45.16%) advanced to the Brazilian runoff election on October 25. Bolsonaro's partial victory boosted the São Paulo stock exchange and the real.

item.title: No Rio, Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro repetem o desempenho da disputa de quatro anos atrás
item.description: The vote between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in Rio de Janeiro largely mirrored the 2022 election, with the same regional split: Lula leading in the South and downtown areas, while Flávio won the West and Southwest zones. The electoral district divisions repeated with minor variations, reflecting the known geographic polarization. Lula’s strongest performance was in the 16th electoral zone, where he secured 64.17% of the votes.

item.title: ‘Todos esperavam’ segundo turno no Brasil, diz secretário de Estado de Trump
item.description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that everyone expected a runoff in the Brazilian presidential election, maintaining a cautious stance without publicly endorsing either Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. President Donald Trump also commented on the Brazilian election results, initially confusing Brazil with India in a social media post before correcting the information.

item.title: Eleições: 9 ex-ministros do governo Lula 3 são eleitos; 12 não conseguem
item.description: Of the 22 former Lula ministers running in the 2026 elections, nine won seats in the first round, including André Fufuca and Rui Costa for the Senate, while twelve failed to secure enough votes. Among those defeated are notable figures like Fernando Haddad and Renan Filho, who ran for state governments, and seven former ministers who competed for Senate seats without success. Performance was stronger in the Chamber of Deputies, where six former ministers secured direct mandates.

item.title: José Dirceu (PT), Janaina Paschoal (PP) e Padre Kelmon (PL): veja candidatos conhecidos que não se elegeram em SP
item.description: Several well-known politicians, including José Dirceu, Janaina Paschoal, and Padre Kelmon, ran again in 2026 but were not elected to the Chamber of Deputies or the São Paulo legislature. Despite receiving tens of thousands of votes, the proportional system did not secure seats for all. The PL led the elections with 17 elected deputies.

item.title: No Rio, Flávio Bolsonaro domina as Zonas Oeste e Sudoeste: veja as maiores votações por bairros
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro voted Sunday morning in Rio de Janeiro at the Escola Municipal Barão Homem de Mello in the North Zone. The article notes he leads the West and Southwest zones of Rio.

item.title: No Rio, Ruas vence em Campo Grande em quatro de cinco zonas que abrangem o bairro; confira
item.description: Douglas Ruas (PL) won in four of the five electoral zones covering Campo Grande in Rio's West Zone, securing 52.64% of the votes against Eduardo Paes's (PSD) 47.36%. In the 246th Zone, Paes achieved the only victory over Ruas among the five districts, with 47.22% of the votes.

item.title: PL é o partido que mais cresce na Câmara; União Brasil encolhe
item.description: The PL became the party with the largest Chamber of Deputies bench after the 2026 elections, winning 121 seats, compared to 46 for União Brasil and 41 for PP. Flávio Bolsonaro led the party's victory by securing 47.03% of the votes in the presidential first round. The composition of Congress remains stable at 513 seats, following the presidential veto on the proposed expansion.

item.title: Lula x Flávio Bolsonaro: veja quem ganhou na sua cidade no mapa de votação do estado do Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads voting in Rio with 53.01%, defeating Lula (PT) who secured 39.41%. The PL candidate won 83 municipalities while Lula only prevailed in 9 cities.

item.title: PL convida eleitos para reunião com Flávio sobre estratégia do 2º turno
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL party, invited the party's bench and elected candidates to a meeting with Flávio Bolsonaro on October 7, 2026, in Brasília, aimed at aligning strategies for the second round of the presidential election. The meeting, set for 3 p.m. at the Juca Chaves Theater, will include prominent party leaders such as governors, senators, and federal deputies. Valdemar also expressed expectations of support from União Brasil, PP, and Republicanos in the runoff, emphasizing the strategic importance of allied parties for electoral success.

item.title: De onde virá o ajuste fiscal prometido por Flávio Bolsonaro?
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) pledges a fiscal adjustment equivalent to 1.5% of GDP, roughly R$204 billion in 2026, but has not detailed how to achieve it. His strategy includes cutting ministries, reducing appointed positions, and revising tax benefits, yet lacks consolidated estimates. The challenge is significant, as mandatory expenditures, especially Social Security, consume most of the budget.

item.title: Áudio: Presidente do TSE faz balanço positivo do primeiro turno das eleições
item.description: TSE president Kássio Nunes Marques evaluated the first round of elections positively, emphasizing transparency and reliability confirmed by international observers. He denied foreign interference and stated voters went to the polls with security and freedom. Abstention reached 21%, and the TSE will work to reduce it in the second round.

item.title: PL elege 121 deputados federais e supera bancada histórica do MDB na Câmara em 1990
item.description: The PL elected 121 federal deputies, becoming the largest bench in the Chamber and surpassing the 1990 MDB record. The victory reflects the growth of the Brazilian right, with figures like Nikolas Ferreira leading the polls and the Bolsonaro family strengthening its presence in the Legislature.

item.title: Quem é Thabatta Pimenta, primeira deputada federal trans do Nordeste
item.description: Thabatta Pimenta, from PV, was elected as the first transgender federal deputy in Rio Grande do Norte with 92,473 votes, becoming the eighth representative of the state in the Chamber of Deputies. Her election marks a historic milestone for LGBTQ+ representation in Northeast Brazil.

item.title: Flávio diz que eleição 'é o fim da era do PT', e Lula diz que 2º turno mostrará 'fotografia real do Brasil'; siga
item.description: Flávio Dória claims the 2026 election signals the end of the PT era, while Lula says the runoff will reveal the true portrait of Brazil. BBC News Brasil provides live coverage of results and analysis from the first round.

item.title: Votos em Garotinho no RJ contam como válidos até decisão final do TSE
item.description: The president of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, ruled that votes for Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos) for governor of Rio de Janeiro will be counted as valid until the plenary reviews the registration of his candidacy. The ruling was issued after the deadline for rejection, keeping the votes pending until a final decision.

item.title: Nikolas consegue eleger bancada de deputados federais e estaduais pelo país
item.description: Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) was reelected federal deputy and became the most-voted candidate in Brazilian history, surpassing Eduardo Bolsonaro's record. His victory helped form a bench of federal and state deputies across the country.

item.title: Apenas oito de 22 ex-ministros do governo Lula vencem nas urnas
item.description: Only 8 of Lula's 22 former ministers were elected to Congress, showing weak legislative performance. Alckmin advances to the presidential runoff with Lula.

item.title: Trump chama Brasil de Índia nas redes e elogia processo eleitoral
item.description: Donald Trump posted on Truth Social congratulating 'India' for the quick announcement of election results, but the message appears to refer to Brazil, since India has not recently held presidential elections and these are indirect in the country. The confusion sparked comments about Trump's relationship with emerging countries. The post highlights U.S. interest in international elections.

item.title: Trump troca Brasil por Índia ao elogiar rapidez na apuração das eleições
item.description: Donald Trump praised the speed of vote counting but seemingly confused Brazil with India when commenting on the Brazilian electoral process on his Truth Social platform. The U.S. president highlighted the quick results in contrast to the American system, causing confusion about which country was being referenced.

item.title: Trump confunde Brasil com Índia ao comentar apuração eleitoral
item.description: Donald Trump confused Brazil with India when commenting on the Brazilian election results, initially posting an incorrect version on his Truth Social profile. The post was later corrected to reference Brazil and used to criticize the U.S. electoral process, alleging fraud without evidence. Trump also advocated for restrictions on mail-in voting ahead of the U.S. midterm elections in November 2026.

item.title: Eleições 2026: quem foi mais votado em Passos (MG) no 1º turno
item.description: In the 2026 elections in Passos (MG), Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) led the vote for president with 51.36%, ahead of Lula (PT) at 38.86%. For governor, Cleitinho Azevedo (REPUBLICANOS) won with 61.56% of the votes. Domingos Savio Campos Resende (PL) was the top Senate candidate with 28.59%, while Diego Rodrigo De Oliveira (PSD) led the five local legislative races.

item.title: Eleições 2026: quem foi mais votado em Pará de Minas (MG) no 1º turno
item.description: In Pará de Minas (MG), presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) led with 62.19% of the votes, followed by Lula (PT) at 27.27%. For governor, Cleitinho Azevedo (REPUBLICANOS) secured 67.88%, while Patrus Ananias (PT) reached 15.49%. In the Senate race, Domingos Savio Campos Resende (PL) was the top vote-getter with 34.53%, and for the federal chamber, Nikolas Ferreira De Oliveira (PL) led with 42.63%.

item.title: Eleições em Nova Serrana (MG): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: In Nova Serrana (MG), Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) led the presidential vote with 71.84%, followed by Lula (PT) with 21.25%. In the state race, Cleitinho Azevedo (REPUBLICANOS) won with 80.58% for governor, while in the Senate, Domingos Savio Campos Resende (PL) secured 39.99% of the votes. The elections took place on October 4, 2026.

item.title: Eleições em Muriaé (MG): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: In Muriaé (MG), the first round of the 2026 elections saw high voter participation with over 71,000 votes counted. Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) led the presidential race with 51.28%, followed by Lula (PT) with 42.14%. In state and federal races, candidates from PL, Republicanos, PSD, and PT also led local preferences.

item.title: Eleições 2026: quem foi mais votado em Coronel Fabriciano (MG) no 1º turno
item.description: In the 2026 elections in Coronel Fabriciano (MG), Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) led the presidential race with 55.80% of the votes, followed by Lula (PT) with 36.92%. For governor, Cleitinho Azevedo (REPUBLICANOS) won with 61.70%, while Domingos Savio Campos Resende (PL) was the most voted Senate candidate with 35.51%.

item.title: Eleições em Conselheiro Lafaiete (MG): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: In Conselheiro Lafaiete (MG), Lula (PT) led the presidential race with 46.31%, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) with 41.95%. For MG governor, Cleitinho Azevedo (REPUBLICANOS) won 49.28%. The 2026 elections include president, governor, senators, and federal and state deputies.

item.title: Eleições em Teixeira de Freitas (BA): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: In Teixeira de Freitas (BA), Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) leads the presidential race with 49.51%, followed by Lula (PT) at 45.39%. Acm Neto (UNIÃO) wins the state race with 56.09%, while Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) secures 43.53%. The results pertain solely to the city's votes and do not determine the national outcome.

item.title: Eleições em Palmas (PR): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: Palmas (PR) held the first round of the 2026 elections for president, state governor, and legislative positions. Jair Bolsonaro (PL) led the presidential race with 49.58%, followed by Lula (PT) with 44.58%. Sergio Moro (PL) led the gubernatorial race with 41.29%.

item.title: Eleições em Rolim de Moura (RO): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: In Rolim de Moura (RO), Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) leads the presidential vote with 70.44%, followed by Lula (PT) with 22.94%. For governor, Marcos Rogério (PL) secured 56.85% of the votes. The 2026 elections feature contests for president, state governor, senate, and federal and state representatives.

item.title: Eleições em Jaru (RO): veja a apuração do 1º turno
item.description: In Jaru (RO), Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) leads the presidential race with 74.17% of the votes, followed by Lula (PT) with 20.03%. Marcos Rogério (PL) wins the state government race with 67%, while Fernando Rodrigues Máximo (PL) and Lucio Antonio Mosquini (PL) lead the Senate and Federal Chamber races, respectively. Luis Eduardo Schincaglia (NOVO) leads for the State Assembly.

item.title: Eleições 2026: quem foi mais votado em Cacoal (RO) no 1º turno
item.description: In Cacoal (RO), Flavio Bolsonaro (PL) led the presidential race with 70.15%, followed by Lula (PT) at 22.48%. For governor, Adailton Furia (PSD) secured 54.88%, while in the Legislative elections, Fernando Rodrigues Máximo (PL) and Joliane Tamires Duran Simões (PSD) stood out. The results reflect only the city's votes and do not determine elected officials.
